textbookText: 6. Many plants are being extinct in Nepal due to climate change. What role can you play to protect such plants? Describe in brief. Ans:- Many plants in Nepal are becoming extinct due to climate change, deforestation, and human negligence. To protect such plants, I can play an important role by participating in tree plantation and conservation programs. I will avoid cutting trees unnecessarily and encourage others to do the same. Creating awareness among local people about the importance of plants and their role in maintaining the balance of nature is also essential. I can help protect rare and medicinal plants by supporting community forest programs and learning about sustainable harvesting methods. By spreading knowledge about the value of biodiversity and taking part in campaigns to preserve forests and herbs, I can contribute to reducing the negative effects of climate change. In this way, every small effort made by individuals can help in conserving the disappearing plant species of Nepal. 7. Study the concept map and answer the following questions. i) White appropriate words in A and B. Ans:- The appropriate words in A is measure of climate change and B is cause of climate change. ii) Give the answers for C, D and E in two points for each. Ans:- Two points for C (manmade cause) are deforestation and industrial pollution. Two points for D ( Natural causes) are volcanic eruptions and solar radiation variation. And two points for E (Effects) are global warming and glacier melting and irregular rainfall and droughts. 8. Observe the given picture thoroughly and explain its role in climate change. Ans:-The given picture is air pollution. Air pollution plays a significant role in climate change by increasing the concentration of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. When fossil fuels such as coal, petrol, and natural gas are burned for energy, they release harmful gases like carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), and nitrous oxide (N₂O). These gases trap the heat from the sun and prevent it from escaping back into space, leading to a rise in the Earth’s average temperature — a process known as the greenhouse effect. Industrial emissions, smoke from vehicles, and burning of waste further add to air pollution, making the atmosphere thicker with heat-trapping gases and particles. In addition to warming the planet, air pollution also affects weather patterns and the balance of ecosystems. For example, pollutants like black carbon (soot) can absorb sunlight and speed up the melting of snow and ice, while aerosols can change rainfall patterns and cloud formation. Moreover, air pollution contributes to smog, acid rain, and poor air quality, which harm both human health and the environment. Therefore, reducing air pollution by using clean energy, controlling industrial emissions, and promoting green transportation is essential to slow down climate change and protect life on Earth. 9. We can find different types of medicinal herbs in our locality. But we depend on others for the treatment of common ailments. Identify the main reason for this and write about what can be done to maximize the use of local medicinal herbs. Ans:- In Nepal, many medicinal herbs such as Tulsi, Neem, Aloe Vera, Ginger, and Turmeric grow naturally in our local areas. However, people still depend on modern medicines and outside sources for the treatment of common ailments. The main reason for this is the lack of proper knowledge and awareness about the identification, use, and benefits of local medicinal herbs. Many traditional healing practices are disappearing as younger generations rely more on modern medical systems and pay less attention to herbal medicine. Additionally, the lack of proper research, documentation, and promotion of medicinal plants has limited their use in daily life. To maximize the use of local medicinal herbs, several steps can be taken. Awareness programs should be conducted in schools and communities to educate people about the importance and safe use of herbal plants. The government and local bodies should encourage the cultivation and conservation of medicinal herbs through community forests and home gardens. Training programs for herbal medicine preparation and proper use can help people treat common diseases locally. Furthermore, promoting traditional knowledge along with scientific research can help preserve Nepal’s rich heritage of herbal medicine and make healthcare more sustainable and affordable for all. 10. By protecting Caterpillar fungus and increasing its production, the economy of the country can also improve. Explain this statement. Ans:- Caterpillar fungus, also known as Yarsagumba, is a valuable medicinal herb found in the high mountainous regions of Nepal. It is often called “Himalayan gold” because it is sold at a very high price in national and international markets. By protecting this fungus and increasing its production, Nepal can earn a large amount of foreign currency through export.
